question: The "Licence Raj" in India during the mid-20th century referred to a system of:
solution:
The correct answer is __**Industrial licensing**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Licence Raj**

 
 
• A system of strict government control and regulation of the Indian economy from the 1950s to the early 1990s.
 
• Businesses required licenses to operate, leading to bureaucratic delays and inefficiencies.
 
• Aimed to protect domestic industries and ensure equitable development.
 
 
 
• **Industrial Licensing**
 
 
• A specific component of the Licence Raj.
 
• Businesses needed licenses to set up new industries or expand existing ones.
 
• The government controlled production capacity, product mix, and location of industries.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Trade Unions**

 
 
• Organizations representing the interests of workers.
 
• Negotiate with employers for better wages, working conditions, and job security.
 
• Play a crucial role in labor relations and social justice.
 
 
 
• **Import Restrictions**
 
 
• Government policies limiting the import of goods to protect domestic industries.
 
• High tariffs and quotas were used to discourage imports.
 
• Aimed at reducing foreign exchange outflow and promoting self-sufficiency.
 
 
 
• **Export Incentives**
 
 
• Government policies encouraging exports to earn foreign exchange.
 
• Tax breaks, subsidies, and other incentives were offered to exporters.
 
• Aimed at boosting export competitiveness and improving the country's balance of payments.
